project_scope.note: All 12 current Euphorbia concepts are already canonical learner taxa. Range labels remain independent from learner inclusion.

taxonomy_notes.legacy_mapping: Several small sandmat species entered the source pool under Chamaesyce; their canonical learner cards retain those names as synonyms but use accepted Euphorbia names.
taxonomy_notes.caution: Do not create duplicate learner cards for legacy Chamaesyce names.

genus_diagnostics.latex: Most learner species exude white milky latex when injured.
genus_diagnostics.cyathium: The apparent 'flower' is a cyathium: a cup-like involucre holding highly reduced male flowers and a central female flower.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: Fruit is typically a three-lobed capsule that separates into three one-seeded units.
genus_diagnostics.showy_parts: In some species the conspicuous white or red structures are bracts, not petals.

shared_traits: tiny cyathia rather than ordinary petaled flowers
bracts, glands, hairs, seed surface, and growth form often matter more than flower color
priority: 1. Growth form: erect showy-bracted plant, upright poinsettia-like herb, or low sandmat.
2. Upper bracts/leaves: broad vs narrow, colored vs green, hairy vs glabrous.
4. Stem/leaf pubescence, especially upper leaf surfaces and abaxial hairs.
5. Mature capsule and seed surface when working in the dentata/davidii or sandmat groups.
study_strategy.warning: Do not identify Euphorbia from overall white/red color alone. Similar-looking species often separate on bract width, hair placement, gland shape, capsule hairs, or mature seed sculpture.

field_groups.look_here_first: Upper-surface hairiness + width/shape of the white-margined bracts.
differences: E. bicolor: narrow linear to narrowly oblanceolate white-margined bracts; upper leaf/bract surfaces conspicuously hairy.
E. marginata: broader elliptic to obovate white-margined bracts; upper leaf surfaces mostly glabrous.

field_groups.look_here_first: Color at the upper bract base, then inspect the cyathial gland opening.
differences: E. cyathophora: upper bracts often sharply colored red/pink/white at the base; gland opening oblong and lacking an annular rim.
E. heterophylla: upper bracts usually green or merely pale; gland opening circular with an annular rim.

field_groups.look_here_first: Mature seed + capsule size + hair texture beneath the leaves.
differences: E. dentata: smaller capsules/seeds; seeds more rounded in cross section and evenly finely tuberculate; hairs generally longer and less stiff.
E. davidii: larger capsules/seeds; seeds more angular with uneven tubercles/wrinkles; hairs shorter, stiffer, often on minute pustular bases.

field_groups.look_here_first: Overall habit first, then stem/leaf hairs, leaf shape/asymmetry, and capsule characters.
differences: E. angusta: narrow leaves; upright to spreading rather than a tight mat.
E. fendleri: low perennial sandmat with a more substantial perennial base.
E. nutans: larger opposite leaves and ascending/erect branching; reddish leaf blotch often present.
E. prostrata: flat radiating annual mat; asymmetric leaf bases; capsules often hairy.
E. serpens: tiny smooth creeping mat; very small rounded leaves; mostly glabrous.
E. villifera: low spreading sandmat with conspicuous soft pubescence.
photo_roles: stem/node and stipule macros where relevant

quick_key.if: erect plant with showy white-margined upper bracts
quick_key.then: Compare Euphorbia bicolor vs E. marginata

quick_key.if: upright poinsettia-like plant with colored or pale upper bracts
quick_key.then: Compare E. cyathophora vs E. heterophylla

quick_key.if: opposite coarsely toothed leaves; green upper plant; dentata-type habit
quick_key.then: Compare E. dentata vs E. davidii

quick_key.if: low creeping/prostrate or small sandmat-like plant
quick_key.then: Use sandmat growth form + hairs + leaves + capsule/seed characters

visual_comparison.title: Euphorbia diagnostic pairs
visual_comparison.subtitle: Compare the closest look-alikes by structure, not overall color.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: White pair: bicolor = narrow + hairy; marginata = broad + mostly glabrous above. Poinsettia pair: cyathophora = colored bract bases + oblong rimless gland; heterophylla = green/pale bracts + round rimmed gland. Dentata pair: seed first — dentata = smaller, rounded, evenly pebbled; davidii = larger, angular, irregularly lumpy. Sandmat trio: prostrata = hairy fruit keels + ridged seed; serpens = glabrous rooted mat + fused stipule scale + smooth seed; villifera = usually erect/ascending + filiform stipules + papillate surfaces.

items.label: Snow-on-the-prairie — narrow + hairy
items.image_role: whole flowering plant / narrow white-margined bracts
items.caption: Start with the narrow white-margined bracts, then confirm conspicuous hairiness on the upper leaf/bract surfaces.
items.creator: Lisa Winnett-Pequeno

items.label: Snow-on-the-mountain — broad + glabrous above
items.caption: Broader white-margined bracts plus upper leaf/bract surfaces that are mostly glabrous separate it from E. bicolor.
items.creator: H. Zell

items.label: Wild poinsettia — colored base + oblong rimless gland
items.caption: Use the sharply white/pink/red bract bases as the first clue, then confirm the single sessile/substipitate gland with an oblong opening and no annular rim.
items.creator: Harry Rose

items.label: Painted spurge — green/pale bracts + round rimmed gland
items.caption: Ignore the highly variable leaf shape. Confirm the stipitate cyathial gland with a circular opening and annular rim.
items.creator: Psumuseum

items.label: Toothed spurge — rounded, evenly pebbled seed
items.caption: This is the strongest tie-breaker. E. dentata has smaller seeds that are rounded in cross section with fine, relatively even tubercles. If seed is absent, check the underside leaf hairs: they are longer, weaker, and non-pustular.
items.creator: S.R. Turner

items.label: David's spurge — angular, irregularly lumpy seed
items.caption: This is the strongest tie-breaker. E. davidii has larger, more angular seeds with irregular low broad tubercles/wrinkles. If seed is absent, check the underside leaf hairs: they are shorter, stiffer, and often arise from minute pustular bases.
items.creator: S.R. Turner

items.label: Prostrate sandmat — hairy fruit keels
items.caption: Usually prostrate/decumbent but not a tightly rooting mat. The strongest confirmation is the capsule: crisped hairs concentrate along the keels and toward the base. Seeds are sharply 4-angled with transverse ridges.
items.creator: Stefan.lefnaer

items.label: Matted sandmat — glabrous rooted mat
items.caption: Strictly prostrate, often rooting at nodes, and essentially glabrous. Look for the conspicuous fused deltate stipule scale; fruit is glabrous and seeds are smooth.
items.creator: Stefan.lefnaer

items.label: Hairy sandmat — filiform stipules + papillate surface
items.image_role: field close-up / opposite leaves, stem, and cyathia
items.caption: Usually erect to ascending rather than a flat mat. Confirm distinct filiform stipules and papillate surfaces. It is usually villous but can be glabrous, so hairiness alone is not safe; capsules are glabrous and often have elongated empty-tipped cocci.
items.creator: UT Austin BIO406D PlantPics

items.label: Nodding spurge — upright + large asymmetric leaves
items.image_role: upper branch / leaves, cyathia and fruit context
items.caption: Start with the much larger ascending/arching habit and opposite oblong serrulate leaves with strongly asymmetric bases. A red central blotch is common but not required; fruit is glabrous.
items.creator: HermannSchachner

items.label: Fendler's sandmat — low woody perennial
items.image_role: Hays County diagnostic composite / habit, leaves and cyathia
items.caption: Think low perennial from a woody crown: clustered glabrous stems, tiny rounded entire leaves, and distinct narrow-linear stipules. Capsule is glabrous; gland-appendage shape is too variable to use alone.
items.creator: UT Austin / Bob Harms

items.label: Narrow-leaf spurge — erect + strigose + linear leaves
items.image_role: whole flowering habit / narrow distal leaves
items.caption: Erect perennial from a thickened rootstock. Distal leaves are linear to elliptic-linear and more than 6× as long as wide; stems, involucre, and capsule are strigose.
items.creator: Alison Northup
